objects.name: Chipkin Example B-ALSC
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. Number_Of_APDU_Retries is served by the app as 3 (12.11.29 suggested default; the stack default of 0 would never retransmit a ConfirmedEventNotification). The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; starts at 21.5. Present_Value is DS-COV-B subscribable (BACnetStack_SetPropertySubscribable); the up/down key feeds subscribers via BACnetStack_UpdateValue

objects.name: Chartreuse
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (canonical: B-SA). commandable; 16-slot Priority_Array, Relinquish_Default 20.0 C, served by GetPropertyReal. Present_Value, Priority_Array and Current_Command_Priority are resolved by the stack from the priority array. ALSO the SCHED-I-B write target - Schedule 1 (Saffron) writes it at priority 8

objects.name: Amber
objects.note: The smoke detector. F-LIFESAFETY / F-ALARM-LS (canonical: B-LSC). Tracking_Value follows the SIMULATED detector (main.cpp section 1b: quiet(0) / alarm(2) / fault(3)); Present_Value LATCHES alarm until a LifeSafetyOperation RESET, which is refused (OBJECT / INVALID_OPERATION_IN_THIS_STATE) while the detector still sees smoke or when nothing is latched; a fault follows the detector and is not latched. Present_Value and Tracking_Value are read-only (Table 12-18). Silenced and Operation_Expected (SILENCE while sounding, RESET once silenced) follow LifeSafetyOperation. Reliability is served by the stack: this example's callback supplies the first stage (cl. 13.2.2.2, hardware - always no-fault-detected here) and the stack's FAULT_LIFE_SAFETY algorithm the second (MULTI_STATE_FAULT while Present_Value is fault). Mode is required-writable and accepted unconditionally (no customer-facing Accepted_Modes setter exists - see the file header); Accepted_Modes is therefore accepted at the stack's generic default. Event_State is NOT actually a stack default here - it is genuinely computed by the CHANGE_OF_LIFE_SAFETY and FAULT_LIFE_SAFETY algorithms this example arms; it is marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know an algorithm was armed (same convention as B-AAC's Diamond). Present_Value is also DS-COV-B subscribable

objects.name: Azure
objects.note: The smoke detector's zone. F-LIFESAFETY / F-ALARM-LS. Rolls up Life Safety Point 1 (Amber): takes its detector reading, latches alarm the same way, and a LifeSafetyOperation addressed to the zone also operates Amber. Event_State is genuinely computed (the same two algorithms are armed on Azure), marked accepted for the same generator-limitation reason. Reliability as Amber's. Zone_Members (cl. 12.16.26, required, BACnetLIST of BACnetDeviceObjectReference) should list Amber but reads as an empty list at 64b2cfac5: the stack serves it, but only the test-tool BACnetStackTestTool_SetLifeSafetyZoneMembers can fill it, and the series does not use the test-tool interface. [KNOWN GAP] in tests/life_safety_test.py; see TODO.md and stack #2036 (open)

objects.name: Crimson
objects.note: Priority, Ack_Required and Recipient_List are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely populated, by BACnetStack_AddNotificationClassObject (Priority, Ack_Required) and BACnetStack_AddRecipientToNotificationClass (Recipient_List) at start-up. They are marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API and so cannot credit them as stack-served. Routes Amber's and Azure's CHANGE_OF_LIFE_SAFETY / fault notifications, CONFIRMED; at start-up to one recipient named by DEVICE instance, 389108, the operator workstation (the stack resolves its address from its I-Am). Recipient_List is registered WRITABLE (BACnetStack_SetPropertyWritable): "limited modification of its alarm and event reporting, including event distribution by another device" (L.5.1); the stack decodes and stores a written list itself. tests/distribution_test.py redirects it

objects.name: Beige
objects.note: F-EVENTLOG (canonical: this repository). AE-EL-I-B. Enable/Buffer_Size/Record_Count/Total_Record_Count/Log_Buffer/Status_Flags/Object_Identifier/Object_Type/Property_List are NOT stack defaults in the generic sense - they are genuinely held and served by the stack's own Event Log engine (BACnetStack_AddEventLogObject), answered from stack storage BEFORE this file's Get*/Set* callbacks are ever consulted; marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know about this object-specific engine. The stack captures every event notification the device itself generates - each life-safety alarm of Amber and Azure is logged once, even when its recipient is unreachable (tests/event_log_test.py reads them back with ReadRange). Enable starts FALSE and the customer interface cannot set it at creation (stack #3301, [KNOWN GAP]); it is writable, so an operator turns logging on. A ReadProperty of Log_Buffer is refused with PROPERTY / READ_ACCESS_DENIED (cl. 12.27.13). BACnetStack_InsertEventLogRecord is test-tool only; this example never fakes a record. Event_State is accepted at the stack's generic default (normal) - no intrinsic reporting is armed on Beige itself

objects.name: Saffron
objects.note: SCHED-I-B (B-AAC-CPP's canonical Saffron). Present_Value, Effective_Period, Schedule_Default, List_Of_Object_Property_References, Priority_For_Writing and Status_Flags are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely held and served by the stack's Schedule engine (BACnetStack_AddScheduleObject plus the BACnetStack_SetSchedule*/AddSchedule* configuration calls in main.cpp); it writes Analog Output 1 (Chartreuse) Present_Value at priority 8. Present_Value, Effective_Period and Priority_For_Writing are marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know about the Schedule engine's own host-configuration API. One weekly transition (Monday 08:00) and one exception that references Calendar 1 Cream are seeded at start-up; the 's' key (common/ 2.1.0's DemoAdvance) adds a transition for right now so the change can be observed without waiting for the wall clock. The engine evaluates against the Device's Local_Date / Local_Time, which the app serves. A TimeSynchronization moves that device clock (tests/schedule_test.py)

objects.name: Cream
objects.note: stack-held (BACnetStack_AddCalendarObject): the stack keeps Date_List - one entry, December 25 of every year (BACnetStack_AddCalendarDateEntry) - and derives Present_Value (TRUE when the Device's Local_Date matches an entry). Schedule 1 Saffron's exception references it

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)
